172	def evaluate_gate(condition, fluents, round_number):
173	    """Supported syntax: "true", "false", or "holdsAt(<fluent_name>)" — true
174	    if any record for that fluent (any holder/args) is currently active."""

4: `state/fluents.json`, one line each: name, then a short description of
5: the concept it represents. The norm-implementer checks this before naming
6: a new fluent — CodeGraph indexes code structure, not string
7: literals, so it won't reliably catch a near-duplicate name for a concept
8: that already exists under a different name. Reuse an existing name for an
9: existing concept; only add an entry here when a round introduces a

15: | `dead` | Permanent — an agent whose running food balance (`runtime["payoff"]`) went negative in `actions/handlers/harvest.py`. Written by the fixed survival mechanic (`engine/physics.py`'s `apply_consumption()`/`is_dead()`), not a norm-implementer mechanism; never terminated once set. Always `visibility="public"`, narration in third person (not "you") since the same string is read by both the affected agent and everyone else it's visible to. |
16: | `rule_active` | The queryable *history* of which `rule_types` entry was actually enforced, for which action, and for how long — `holder="community"`, `args={"action": "<action_name>", "type": "<the rule_types key>"}` (a dict, not a list — the one deliberate exception to every other fluent's `args` shape, since a rule type has no single agent to key off, and needs both action+type to be unique since a type_name is only unique within its own action's rule directory). Opened via `set_fact()` the same round `state/config.json`'s `"rules"[action_name]` list activates a type, closed via `end_fact()` the round it's removed/replaced (or automatically, on natural lifecycle expiry — see `engine.institution.rules.tick_rule_lifecycles()`) — this is what actually answers "was this rule in force during round N for this action," which `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog (static: what types *exist*) deliberately does not track. Never confuse the two: `rule_types` changes only when a genuinely new shape is invented; `rule_active` changes every time a round's config activates, deactivates, or a rule's own duration expires one. |

197	    """Rules (actions/rules/harvest/*.py, orchestrated by a harvest-scoped
198	    RuleSet — engine/institution/rules.py) enforce themselves by
199	    reducing/zeroing an agent's harvested_kg (a cap, a ban, a reserve
200	    draw) — this is what makes sure the affected agent actually learns
201	    that, rather than only ever seeing the resulting kg number with no way
202	    to tell an enforced outcome apart from one they freely chose. A rule's
203	    own after_agent()-patched note (round_record["agents"][agent_id]
204	    ["note"]) is preferred verbatim when a rule authored one — it's the
205	    specific, in-world sentence that rule chose (an over-cap trim, a
206	    reserve top-up). Falls back to a generic derived sentence when no rule
207	    bothered to explain itself: catch_from_effort() is pure and
208	    mechanism-agnostic, so re-running it on the agent's own recorded
209	    effort against that round's starting stock gives what their effort
210	    alone would have produced with nothing else in play. If the agent
211	    wasn't even asked that round (a live ban, via some rule's own
212	    is_eligible() hook — not something inferable from numbers alone),
213	    "participated": False is set explicitly by actions/handlers/harvest.py;
214	    anything else defaults to participated.
215	    """
216	    if mine_record.get("participated") is False:
217	        return " You weren't able to fish at all this round — something about the community's current rules held you back."

219	    if mine_record.get("note"):
220	        return f" {mine_record['note'].strip()}"
221	
222	    baseline_kg = catch_from_effort(mine_record["effort"], entry["stock_kg_before"])
223	    shortfall = baseline_kg - mine_record["harvested_kg"]
224	    if shortfall > max(0.5, 0.05 * baseline_kg):
225	        return (
226	            f" That's less than your effort alone would normally have brought in "
227	            f"(more like {baseline_kg:.0f}kg) — something about the community's "
228	            f"current rules held some of it back."

186	    """The default `args=None` (-> `[agent_id]`) is correct only for a role
187	    every eligible agent holds *simultaneously and independently* (e.g.
188	    "fisher" — one open record per agent, all coexisting on purpose).
189	
190	    For a role only one agent holds *at a time* (a rotating recorder,
191	    steward, monitor), pass `exclusive=True` instead of trying to get
192	    `args` right yourself — set_fact()'s own termination logic only closes
193	    a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
194	    plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
195	    assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
196	    previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
197	    holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
198	    then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
199	    silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
200	    a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
201	    that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
202	    than something the caller has to remember to get right.
203	
204	    `narration`/`visibility`/`event_type` let a role grant also be a
205	    visible, memory-worthy event (e.g. "Kai has become the pot keeper") —
206	    same contract as `set_fact()`, since this is just its role-shaped
207	    convenience wrapper; previously always silent (`narration=None`)."""
208	    resolved_args = [] if exclusive else (args if args is not None else [agent_id])

196	def _harvest_shortfall_clause(mine_record, entry):
197	    """Rules (actions/rules/harvest/*.py, orchestrated by a harvest-scoped
198	    RuleSet — engine/institution/rules.py) enforce themselves by
199	    reducing/zeroing an agent's harvested_kg (a cap, a ban, a reserve
200	    draw) — this is what makes sure the affected agent actually learns
201	    that, rather than only ever seeing the resulting kg number with no way
202	    to tell an enforced outcome apart from one they freely chose. A rule's
203	    own after_agent()-patched note (round_record["agents"][agent_id]
204	    ["note"]) is preferred verbatim when a rule authored one — it's the
205	    specific, in-world sentence that rule chose (an over-cap trim, a
206	    reserve top-up). Falls back to a generic derived sentence when no rule
207	    bothered to explain itself: catch_from_effort() is pure and
208	    mechanism-agnostic, so re-running it on the agent's own recorded
209	    effort against that round's starting stock gives what their effort
210	    alone would have produced with nothing else in play. If the agent
211	    wasn't even asked that round (a live ban, via some rule's own
212	    is_eligible() hook — not something inferable from numbers alone),
213	    "participated": False is set explicitly by actions/handlers/harvest.py;
214	    anything else defaults to participated.
215	    """
216	    if mine_record.get("participated") is False:
217	        return " You weren't able to fish at all this round — something about the community's current rules held you back."
218	
219	    if mine_record.get("note"):
220	        return f" {mine_record['note'].strip()}"
221	
222	    baseline_kg = catch_from_effort(mine_record["effort"], entry["stock_kg_before"])
223	    shortfall = baseline_kg - mine_record["harvested_kg"]
224	    if shortfall > max(0.5, 0.05 * baseline_kg):
225	        return (
226	            f" That's less than your effort alone would normally have brought in "
227	            f"(more like {baseline_kg:.0f}kg) — something about the community's "
228	            f"current rules held some of it back."
229	        )
230	    return ""

    description = "Enforce daily catch cap of 20% of current stock"

        # Compute daily total for this agent (this rule runs per-agent after harvest)

        stock = ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"]

            record_entry["note"] = (existing + " " + note).strip()
            # Fine 5 kg from ledger for any excess
            ctx.objects.withdraw("communal_ledger", "balance_kg", 5.0, by_agent_id=agent_id,

2	regardless of what any norm asks for. Ported directly from Gupta et al.'s
3	CPR-game codebase (Codes/Gupta/CPRG_fishing, branch origin/hiromu/llm-norm,
4	ostrom3/Agent.py and Model.py), not this project's own design — a norm can
5	change caps, deposits, bans, and schedules (all implementer-owned, in
6	actions/rules/ and actions/), but the underlying catch equation, regrowth
7	rate, and survival economics below are the fixed rules of the world those
8	choices play out against, not something a community vote should be able
9	to rewrite.
10	
11	Lives under engine/ specifically so it's outside the norm-implementer's
12	permission.edit allowlist (actions/rules/*/*, actions/*, prompts/*, plus a
13	few named files) by construction, the same way engine/simulate.py and
14	engine/llm_agents.py already are. The rate constants below live here for
15	the same reason the equations do, not in state/config.json (which the
16	norm-implementer can freely edit) — a fixed formula reading a
17	norm-implementer-editable rate is exactly as rewritable as the formula
18	itself would be.
19	
20	`available_stock()` moved in from the old `mechanisms/stock_check.py`
21	(2026-09-09, when `mechanisms/` was renamed to `roles/` and reserved for
22	role/fluent code only) — it's a trivial one-line accessor, but it's fixed
23	protected infrastructure exactly like everything else here, not
24	role-related, so it belongs next to the physics it reads alongside.
25	"""
26	
27	HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
28	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
29	CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
30	CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by
31	
32	
33	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
39	
40	
41	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
49	
50	
51	def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
52	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
53	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
54	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
55	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
56	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
58	
59	
60	def is_dead(payoff):
61	    """Matches Gupta et al.'s `if self.payoff < 0: self.dead = True` —
62	    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
63	    return payoff < 0
64	
65

67	    """The agent_id iteration order every action should use, not
68	    state["agents"] directly — excludes anyone in runtime["dead_agents"].
69	    One shared helper so death exclusion can't be forgotten by an action
70	    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per action could be."""
71	    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
72	    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]

34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY

42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)

3	CPR-game codebase (Codes/Gupta/CPRG_fishing, branch origin/hiromu/llm-norm,
4	ostrom3/Agent.py and Model.py), not this project's own design — a norm can
5	change caps, deposits, bans, and schedules (all implementer-owned, in
6	actions/rules/ and actions/), but the underlying catch equation, regrowth
7	rate, and survival economics below are the fixed rules of the world those
8	choices play out against, not something a community vote should be able
9	to rewrite.
10	
11	Lives under engine/ specifically so it's outside the norm-implementer's
12	permission.edit allowlist (actions/rules/*/*, actions/*, prompts/*, plus a
13	few named files) by construction, the same way engine/simulate.py and
14	engine/llm_agents.py already are. The rate constants below live here for
15	the same reason the equations do, not in state/config.json (which the
16	norm-implementer can freely edit) — a fixed formula reading a
17	norm-implementer-editable rate is exactly as rewritable as the formula
18	itself would be.
19	
20	`available_stock()` moved in from the old `mechanisms/stock_check.py`
21	(2026-09-09, when `mechanisms/` was renamed to `roles/` and reserved for
22	role/fluent code only) — it's a trivial one-line accessor, but it's fixed
23	protected infrastructure exactly like everything else here, not
24	role-related, so it belongs next to the physics it reads alongside.
25	"""
26	
27	HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
28	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
29	CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
30	CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by
31	
32	
33	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
39	
40	
41	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
49	
50	
51	def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
52	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
53	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
54	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
55	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
56	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
58	
59	
60	def is_dead(payoff):
61	    """Matches Gupta et al.'s `if self.payoff < 0: self.dead = True` —
62	    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
63	    return payoff < 0
64	
65	
66	def alive_agent_ids(agents, runtime):
67	    """The agent_id iteration order every action should use, not
68	    state["agents"] directly — excludes anyone in runtime["dead_agents"].
69	    One shared helper so death exclusion can't be forgotten by an action
70	    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per action could be."""
71	    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
72	    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]
73	
74	
75	def available_stock(runtime):
76	    return runtime["stock_kg"]

3	class TripCapRule(Rule):
4	    type_name = "trip_cap"
5	    description = "Enforce per-trip catch cap of 15 kg"
6	
7	    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
8	        cap = self.params.get("cap_kg", 15.0)
9	        harvested = record_entry.get("harvested_kg", 0.0)
10	        if harvested > cap:
11	            # Trim to cap and note violation
12	            record_entry["harvested_kg"] = cap
13	            note = f"Trip cap applied: harvested reduced to {cap:.1f} kg."
14	            # Append note
15	            existing = record_entry.get("note") or ""
16	            record_entry["note"] = (existing + " " + note).strip()
17	            # Fine 5 kg from ledger
18	            ctx.objects.withdraw("communal_ledger", "balance_kg", 5.0, by_agent_id=agent_id,
19	                narration=f"Fine for exceeding trip cap applied to {agent_id}.")
20	        return record_entry

24	from engine.institution.registry import discover_subclasses

26	
27	class Rule:
28	    """Base class for one entry under actions/rules/{action_name}/. Every
29	    hook is optional (all default to a no-op) — implement only the ones a
30	    given rule actually needs. `self.key`/`self.params` mirror the old
31	    Norm contract exactly (never persist anything on self between hooks;
32	    a fresh instance is built every round — use ctx.rule_state(self.key)
33	    for anything that must survive across rounds)."""
34	
35	    type_name: str = None  # set by every subclass; unique within its own action's rule directory
36	
37	    def __init__(self, key, params):
38	        self.key = key
39	        self.params = params
40	
41	    # --- round-level: fires once per round, independent of any one action ---
42	
43	    def before_round(self, state, round_number):
44	        """Once per round, before ANY action in this round's schedule has
45	        run. `state` is the full round-state dict (no single ActionContext
46	        exists yet at this point — nothing has been resolved to one
47	        action's participants)."""
48	        return None
49	
50	    def after_round(self, state, round_number):
51	        """Once per round, after EVERY action in this round's schedule has
52	        already run."""
53	        return None
54	
55	    # --- action-level: fires once per round for this rule's own action ---
56	
57	    def before_action(self, ctx):
58	        """Once, before this action's own participants are processed this
59	        round. `ctx` is the action's ActionContext."""
60	        return None
61	
62	    def after_action(self, ctx, round_record):
63	        """Once, after this action's round_record has been fully built —
64	        may mutate `round_record` and/or `ctx.state` directly (a stock
65	        override, a tally adjustment, a community-wide consequence). This
66	        is where a "the whole action's outcome" rule belongs, as opposed
67	        to a per-agent one."""
68	        return None
69	
70	    # --- per-agent: only meaningful for an action whose handler calls
71	    # these explicitly inside its own per-agent loop (every handler in
72	    # this project does, including the generic Level-2 path) ---
73	
74	    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
75	        """False skips this agent's LLM call entirely this round (a live
76	        ban). Called at most once per agent per round."""
77	        return True
78	
79	    def describe(self, ctx, agent_id):
80	        """One already-in-world-phrased sentence describing whatever this
81	        rule currently has to say to this agent, or None. Every active
82	        rule's non-None output is joined into one constraints line."""
83	        return None
84	
85	    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
86	        """Once per participating agent, right after their own
87	        record_entry dict has been built from their response — return a
88	        dict of fields to merge onto it (e.g. {"harvested_kg": 12.0,
89	        "note": "trimmed to the 15kg limit"}), or None for no change.
90	        Multiple rules run in state["config"]["rules"][action] order, each
91	        seeing the previous rule's already-applied patch on
92	        `record_entry` — this is the ordering-dependent chain (a reserve
93	        rule seeing a cap rule's already-trimmed number) the old
94	        raw_kg/proposed_kg threading provided; a rule needing the
95	        pre-any-rule original value re-derives it from a field no rule
96	        touches (harvest's own "effort" field, say), the same technique
97	        `engine.llm_agents._harvest_shortfall_clause()` already uses."""
98	        return None
99	
100	    def on_agent_settled(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
101	        """Once per agent, after EVERY rule's after_agent() has already
102	        applied its patch — `record_entry` here is the fully-settled
103	        final state, not the intermediate view after_agent() sees mid-chain.
104	        For a side effect that must react to the final outcome rather than
105	        any one rule's own contribution to it (starting a ban countdown
106	        because the settled record turned out to be a violation, say).
107	        Return value is ignored — this hook is for side effects
108	        (ctx.rule_state(self.key), ctx.objects, ctx.events), never for
109	        further patching record_entry itself; use after_agent() for that."""
110	        return None

1	# ObjectRuntime: the institutional-object layer (pools, ledgers, tools).
2	# Backed by three things, deliberately kept as separate as
3	# state/config.json's rules are from their own runtime state:
4	#
5	#   - state/object_types/*.json — the declarative ObjectSpec (ownership/
6	#     fields/operations/permissions/visibility). Ships empty by default,
7	#     same "no seed content" principle as actions/rules/.
8	#   - state/objects.json — DECLARATIONS only ({"id", "type", "lifecycle"?}),
9	#     norm-implementer-owned, exactly like state/config.json["rules"][action_name]'s
10	#     own entries — never mutated by the running simulation.
11	#   - state["runtime"]["objects"][object_id]["fields"] — the actual mutable
12	#     field values, simulation-owned, mirroring runtime["rules"][key]'s own
13	#     role as a rule's cross-round-persistent state. Lazily seeded from the
14	#     type's own field defaults the first time an object is touched.
15	#
16	# Conflating declaration and mutable state in one implementer-writable file
17	# is exactly the failure shape this project's config.json/runtime.json
18	# split already exists to avoid — see CLAUDE.md's own history for why
19	# state/runtime.json stays off the norm-implementer's tracked paths.
20	#
21	# Every generic operation (deposit/withdraw/set/append/read) is
22	# permission-checked against the object type's own declared `permissions`;
23	# a type may also name a `custom_handler` (a filename stem under
24	# objects/handlers/, the Level-3 escape hatch) for behavior the five
25	# generic operations can't express — that handler is responsible for its
26	# own permission checking, since it isn't one of the fixed operations
27	# OPERATION_PERMISSION knows about.
28	#
29	# A mutation never itself becomes a fact — a field's current value is
30	# read live (via read(), which already applies the type's own per-field
31	# visibility), not cached as a fact that could go stale. Only the
32	# *announcement* of a mutation (when the caller supplies `narration`)
33	# becomes an Event (state/events.json, via ctx.events.emit() — see
34	# engine.institution.events), so it reaches render_notices()/memory for
35	# exactly the round it happened and never lingers.

72	    def _fields(self, object_id, spec):
73	        """The mutable field dict for this object, lazily seeded from the
74	        type's own declared defaults on first touch — never pre-populated
75	        by a norm-implementer edit to state/objects.json itself."""

77	        fields = record.setdefault("fields", {})

82	    def _check_permission(self, object_id, spec, permission_key, agent_id):
83	        rule = spec.get("permissions", {}).get(permission_key, {"who": "ALL"})
84	        who = rule.get("who", "ALL")
85	        if who == "ALL":
86	            return
87	        if who == "NONE":
88	            raise ObjectPermissionError(f"{permission_key} on {object_id!r} is never permitted")
89	        if who.startswith("ROLE:"):

91	            holder = current_holder(self.fluents, role_name, self.round_number)
92	            if agent_id is None or holder != agent_id:
93	                raise ObjectPermissionError(
94	                    f"{permission_key} on {object_id!r} requires the {role_name!r} role; "
95	                    f"{agent_id!r} does not hold it"
96	                )
97	            return
98	        raise ValueError(f"unrecognized permission rule {who!r}")

106	    def _add(self, object_id, field, delta, operation, by_agent_id, narration):
107	        declaration = self._declaration(object_id)
108	        spec = self._spec(declaration)
109	        self._check_permission(object_id, spec, OPERATION_PERMISSION[operation], by_agent_id)
110	        fields = self._fields(object_id, spec)
111	        fields[field] = fields.get(field, 0) + delta
112	        self._announce(object_id, spec, narration)
113	        return fields[field]

116	        declaration = self._declaration(object_id)
117	        spec = self._spec(declaration)
118	        self._check_permission(object_id, spec, OPERATION_PERMISSION["set"], by_agent_id)
119	        fields = self._fields(object_id, spec)
120	        fields[field] = value
121	        self._announce(object_id, spec, narration)
122	        return fields[field]
123	
124	    def append(self, object_id, field, value, by_agent_id=None, narration=None):
125	        declaration = self._declaration(object_id)
126	        spec = self._spec(declaration)
127	        self._check_permission(object_id, spec, OPERATION_PERMISSION["append"], by_agent_id)
128	        fields = self._fields(object_id, spec)
129	        fields.setdefault(field, []).append(value)
130	        self._announce(object_id, spec, narration)
131	        return fields[field]

133	    def read(self, object_id, field, viewer_agent_id=None):
134	        """Returns None if `field` isn't visible to `viewer_agent_id` per
135	        the object type's own `visibility` rules — never raises, since a
136	        field simply not being visible to a particular viewer is a normal
137	        outcome (this is what a Level-2 action's own prompt.fields
138	        resolution calls to decide what to surface), not a misuse the way
139	        an out-of-scope write is."""
140	        declaration = self._declaration(object_id)
141	        spec = self._spec(declaration)
142	        rule = spec.get("visibility", {}).get(field, {"who": "ALL"})
143	        who = rule.get("who", "ALL")
144	        fields = self._fields(object_id, spec)
145	        if who == "ALL":
146	            return fields.get(field)
147	        if who == "NONE":
148	            return None
149	        if who.startswith("ROLE:"):
150	            role_name = who.split(":", 1)[1]
151	            holder = current_holder(self.fluents, role_name, self.round_number)
152	            return fields.get(field) if holder == viewer_agent_id else None
153	        raise ValueError(f"unrecognized visibility rule {who!r}")
154	
155	    def custom(self, object_id, operation, by_agent_id=None, **kwargs):
156	        """Dispatches to `objects/handlers/{custom_handler}.py`'s `run`
157	        function for a type that declares one — the Level-3 escape hatch
158	        for behavior the five generic operations above can't express. The
159	        handler receives this runtime, the object_id, the operation name,
160	        and every kwarg, and is responsible for its own permission
161	        checking (it isn't in OPERATION_PERMISSION's fixed map)."""
162	        declaration = self._declaration(object_id)
163	        spec = self._spec(declaration)
164	        handler_name = spec.get("custom_handler")
165	        if not handler_name:
166	            raise ValueError(f"{declaration['type']!r} declares no custom_handler")
167	        import objects.handlers as handlers_package
168	
169	        handler = discover_handlers(handlers_package).get(handler_name)
170	        if handler is None:
171	            raise ValueError(f"no objects/handlers/{handler_name}.py exposing run(ctx)")
172	        return handler(self, object_id, operation, by_agent_id=by_agent_id, **kwargs)
173	
174	    def _announce(self, object_id, spec, narration):
175	        if narration is None:
176	            return
177	        event_type = spec.get("memory_policy", {}).get("on_mutate_event_type", "object_mutated")
178	        self.events.emit(Event(event_type=event_type, text=narration, visibility=Visibility.GLOBAL))

794	    """Every action's own spec file, and its handler file (if it names one

class DailyCapRule(Rule):
    type_name = "daily_cap"
    description = "Enforce daily catch cap of 20% of current stock"

    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        # Compute daily total for this agent (this rule runs per-agent after harvest)
        # We'll need to accumulate across agents via a shared state key
        daily_key = f"daily_total_{agent_id}"
        total = ctx.rule_state(daily_key).get("total", 0.0)
        total += record_entry.get("harvested_kg", 0.0)

        # Determine cap based on current stock
        stock = ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"]
        cap = 0.20 * stock
        if total > cap:
            # Trim the current agent's contribution to respect cap proportionally
            excess = total - cap
            # Reduce this agent's record proportionally
            reduction = min(record_entry.get("harvested_kg", 0.0), excess)
            record_entry["harvested_kg"] -= reduction
            note = f"Daily cap applied: reduced by {reduction:.1f} kg to meet 20% stock limit."
            existing = record_entry.get("note", "")
            record_entry["note"] = (existing + " " + note).strip()
            # Fine 5 kg from ledger for any excess

    group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
    agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
    return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}

    steward, monitor), pass `exclusive=True` instead of trying to get
    `args` right yourself — set_fact()'s own termination logic only closes
    a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
    plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
    assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
    previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
    holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
    then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
    silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
    a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
    that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
    than something the caller has to remember to get right.

    visible, memory-worthy event (e.g. "Kai has become the pot keeper") —
    same contract as `set_fact()`, since this is just its role-shaped
    convenience wrapper; previously always silent (`narration=None`)."""
